en: Hetusahetukaduka (The Dyad on Conditions and Having Conditions)
Dependent on a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor non-root, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither non-root nor not-a-root, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor non-root, and [a state that is] neither non-root...

Both states that possess a cause and are not themselves causes arise by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that possesses a cause and is not itself a cause, a state that neither possesses a cause nor is a cause arises by way of the root-condition. They arise by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on a state that is both with-root and not itself a root, there arise states that are both not-root and not-with-root, and states that are both not-with-root and not-not-root, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root and with-root, and dependent on a state that is both with-root and not itself a root, [there arise] states that are both not-root and not-with-root...

And a state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, and also a state that is accompanied by a root but is not a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, and also a state that is accompanied by a root but is not a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, and a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root.
And various states arise with a cause as their condition by way of root-cause.
